syscon_signals.name: CLK_O
syscon_signals.semantics: System clock output generated by SYSCON. Coordinates all activities for the internal logic within the WISHBONE interconnect.

syscon_signals.name: RST_O
syscon_signals.semantics: Reset output generated by SYSCON. Forces all WISHBONE interfaces to restart. All internal self-starting state machines forced into initial state. Active HIGH (per RULE 2.30).

common_master_slave_signals.name: CLK_I
common_master_slave_signals.semantics: Clock input. All WISHBONE output signals registered at rising edge of CLK_I; all input signals stable before rising edge of CLK_I.

common_master_slave_signals.name: DAT_I()
common_master_slave_signals.semantics: Data input array. Used to pass binary data. Array boundaries determined by the port size (max 64 bits, e.g. DAT_I(63..0)).

common_master_slave_signals.name: DAT_O()
common_master_slave_signals.semantics: Data output array. Used to pass binary data. Array boundaries determined by the port size (max 64 bits, e.g. DAT_O(63..0)).

common_master_slave_signals.name: RST_I
common_master_slave_signals.semantics: Reset input. Forces the WISHBONE interface to restart. All internal self-starting state machines forced to initial state. Active HIGH.

common_master_slave_signals.name: TGD_I()
common_master_slave_signals.semantics: Data tag type, input. Associated with DAT_I() and qualified by STB_I. User-defined (parity, ECC, time stamp, etc.). Optional.

common_master_slave_signals.name: TGD_O()
common_master_slave_signals.semantics: Data tag type, output. Associated with DAT_O() and qualified by STB_O. User-defined. Optional.

master_signals.name: ACK_I
master_signals.semantics: Acknowledge input. When asserted, indicates the normal termination of a bus cycle.

master_signals.name: ADR_O()
master_signals.semantics: Address output array. Higher boundary is specific to the address width of the core; lower boundary determined by data port size and granularity (e.g. on a 32-bit BYTE-granularity port, ADR_O(n..2)). On FIFO-like interfaces the array may not be present.

master_signals.name: CYC_O
master_signals.semantics: Cycle output. When asserted, indicates a valid bus cycle is in progress. Asserted for the duration of all bus cycles. During BLOCK transfer cycle there can be multiple data transfers — CYC_O is asserted during the first data transfer and remains asserted until the last data transfer. Useful for multi-port interfaces (dual-port memories) — requests use of a common bus from an arbiter.

master_signals.name: STALL_I
master_signals.semantics: Pipeline stall input. Indicates that the current slave is not able to accept the transfer in the transaction queue. Used in pipelined mode.

master_signals.name: ERR_I
master_signals.semantics: Error input. Indicates an abnormal cycle termination. The source of the error and the response generated by the MASTER are defined by the IP core supplier.

master_signals.name: LOCK_O
master_signals.semantics: Lock output. When asserted, indicates the current bus cycle is uninterruptible. Lock is asserted to request complete ownership of the bus. Once the transfer has started, INTERCON does not grant the bus to any other MASTER until current MASTER negates LOCK_O or CYC_O.

master_signals.name: RTY_I
master_signals.semantics: Retry input. Indicates that the interface is not ready to accept or send data, and that the cycle should be retried. When and how the cycle is retried is defined by the IP core supplier.

master_signals.name: SEL_O()
master_signals.semantics: Select output array. Indicates where valid data is expected on DAT_I() during READ cycles, and where it is placed on DAT_O() during WRITE cycles. Array boundaries determined by the granularity of the port (e.g. 8-bit granularity on 64-bit port -> SEL_O(7..0)). Each SEL_O bit correlates to one active byte lane.

master_signals.name: STB_O
master_signals.semantics: Strobe output. Indicates a valid data transfer cycle. Used to qualify SEL_O(), ADR_O(), DAT_O(), WE_O, TAGN_O. SLAVE asserts ACK_I, ERR_I, or RTY_I in response to every assertion of STB_O.

master_signals.name: TGA_O()
master_signals.semantics: Address tag type. Contains information associated with ADR_O(); qualified by STB_O. E.g. address size (24-bit, 32-bit), memory management (protected vs unprotected).

master_signals.name: TGC_O()
master_signals.semantics: Cycle tag type. Contains information associated with bus cycles; qualified by CYC_O. Used to discriminate between SINGLE/BLOCK/RMW cycles, or to mark interrupt-acknowledge / cache-control cycles.

master_signals.name: WE_O
master_signals.semantics: Write enable output. Indicates whether the current local bus cycle is a READ (WE_O=0) or WRITE (WE_O=1) cycle.

master_signals.name: CTI_O()
master_signals.semantics: Cycle Type Identifier Address Tag. 000=Classic, 001=Constant address burst, 010=Incrementing burst, 011-110=Reserved, 111=End-of-Burst. Optional Registered Feedback signal.

master_signals.name: BTE_O()
master_signals.semantics: Burst Type Extension Address Tag. 00=Linear, 01=4-beat wrap, 10=8-beat wrap, 11=16-beat wrap. Used with CTI_O()=incrementing burst.

slave_signals.name: ACK_O
slave_signals.semantics: Acknowledge output. When asserted, indicates the termination of a normal bus cycle.

slave_signals.name: ADR_I()
slave_signals.semantics: Address input array. Higher boundary is specific to the address width of the core. May not be present on FIFO-like interfaces.

slave_signals.name: CYC_I
slave_signals.semantics: Cycle input. When asserted, indicates a valid bus cycle is in progress. SLAVE only responds when CYC_I is asserted.

slave_signals.name: STALL_O
slave_signals.semantics: Pipeline stall output. Indicates the slave cannot accept additional transactions in its queue. Pipelined mode only.

slave_signals.name: ERR_O
slave_signals.semantics: Error output. Indicates an abnormal cycle termination. Conditions defined by IP core supplier.

slave_signals.name: LOCK_I
slave_signals.semantics: Lock input. When asserted, indicates the current bus cycle is uninterruptible. A SLAVE that receives the LOCK_I signal is accessed by a single MASTER only, until either LOCK_I or CYC_I is negated.

slave_signals.name: RTY_O
slave_signals.semantics: Retry output. Indicates that the interface is not ready to accept or send data, and that the cycle should be retried.

slave_signals.name: SEL_I()
slave_signals.semantics: Select input array. Indicates where valid data is placed on DAT_I() during WRITE cycles, and where it should be present on DAT_O() during READ cycles.

slave_signals.name: STB_I
slave_signals.semantics: Strobe input. When asserted, indicates that the SLAVE is selected. SLAVE responds to other WISHBONE signals only when STB_I is asserted (except for RST_I which is always responded to). SLAVE asserts ACK_O, ERR_O, or RTY_O in response to every STB_I assertion.

slave_signals.name: TGA_I()
slave_signals.semantics: Address tag input. Contains information associated with ADR_I(); qualified by STB_I.

slave_signals.name: TGC_I()
slave_signals.semantics: Cycle tag input. Contains information associated with bus cycles; qualified by CYC_I.

slave_signals.name: WE_I
slave_signals.semantics: Write enable input. Indicates whether the current local bus cycle is READ (WE_I=0) or WRITE (WE_I=1).

slave_signals.name: CTI_I()
slave_signals.semantics: Cycle Type Identifier input. 000/001/010/111 etc. Optional Registered Feedback signal.

slave_signals.name: BTE_I()
slave_signals.semantics: Burst Type Extension input. Optional Registered Feedback signal.

handshake_pairs.stb_ack_standard: MASTER asserts STB_O; SLAVE responds with ACK_O / ERR_O / RTY_O (driven by logical AND of CYC_I AND STB_I). At every rising CLK_I, the terminating signal is sampled.
handshake_pairs.cyc_stb_pair: CYC_O qualifies the whole cycle; STB_O qualifies each phase within the cycle; CYC_O asserted no later than first STB_O and negated no earlier than last STB_O.
handshake_pairs.stall_pipelined: Pipelined mode: SLAVE STALL_O asserted to throttle MASTER; MASTER holds STB_O / request signals until STALL_I=0.

dependency_graph.wishbone_common_rule: SLAVE samples ADR_I(), DAT_I(), SEL_I(), WE_I, TGA_I(), TGD_I(), TGC_I() only when CYC_I=1 AND STB_I=1. SLAVE drives DAT_O() qualified by ACK_O / ERR_O / RTY_O.
dependency_graph.wishbone_pipelining: MASTER asserts STB_O+CYC_O for each new request; SLAVE asserts STALL_O to throttle; ACKs come back in order after the slave-pipeline completes.
dependency_graph.wishbone_state_machine: MASTER: IDLE -> STROBE -> WAIT_TERMINATION -> NEXT_PHASE_or_IDLE. SLAVE: IDLE -> DECODE (samples on STB_I+CYC_I) -> RESPOND (drive ACK_O/ERR_O/RTY_O + data) -> IDLE on STB_I negation.

ordering_rules.wishbone_classic_standard: Strictly in-order — handshake protocol implies one outstanding transfer at a time.
ordering_rules.wishbone_classic_pipelined: FIFO pipeline order — requests issued in order, ACKs returned in order.
ordering_rules.wishbone_block_burst_order: All beats of a BLOCK or Registered Feedback burst are sequential; address increments per Section 3.5 (Linear/Wrap-4/Wrap-8/Wrap-16) for incrementing bursts.
ordering_rules.wishbone_multi_master_order: Multi-MASTER ordering is INTERCON-arbiter-defined; user-defined arbitration policy (priority / round-robin / etc.).
